subject: reduce rate of plot redraws or ignore numeric spinner until released

messages.author: c44317922efa0f6c
messages.subject: reduce rate of plot redraws or ignore numeric spinner until released
parts:
Hi,


This is pretty much a question I've just asked on the coursera data products course, but I thought I might have a better chance of an answer here.


I have a plot in a shiny app that takes a little while to redraw, it's <1s, but a noticeable time. This plot is dependent on some numeric input values. If you adjust these by holding down the spinner (up/down) buttons it looks like flushes build up for each value you go through. This means when you release the button the plot continues to redraw itself, apparently going through each value that the numeric input did. Responsiveness not great...


Roughly:

mydata <- reactive({myfunction(myinput(), input$value, ...)})
myplot <- reactive({
    localdata <- mydata()
    #... do stuff to localdata
    qplot(xval,yval,data=localdata)
})
output$outplot <- renderPlot({myplot()})

There are other dependencies in there, but this is the only place input$value appears. I've tried various things with isolate() and priorities, but can't stop it happening (unless myplot is never updated). I don't want the plot to update until the spinner is released, it should redraw only once. Any idea how to do that? I know a separate 'update' button is an option, but would like to try to avoid it. Been looking at suspend, but don't think it will help. The right solution would probably be to only fire the flush on release of the spinner button, but that would require customisation of the input element. I've been wondering if an invalidateLater observer that updates a reactiveValues object with the input values when they change would work to insulate the plot from individual updates and allow me to control the redraw frequency without forcing a redraw every n seconds. Alternatively, any way to drop new flushes for a dead period after a redraw (ideally while redrawing once at the end of that period)?


Thanks for your time.

--

imalone

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: reduce rate of plot redraws or ignore numeric spinner until released
parts:
You're right that letting you customize the debounce/throttle rate of the spinner would be the best solution. In the meantime, take a look at this gist: https://gist.github.com/jcheng5/6141ea7066e62cafb31c

You can copy that code into your server.R or global.R, and then use it to wrap the input$value. For example:

debouncedValue <- debounce({input$value}, 500)
mydata <- reactive({myfunction(myinput(), debouncedValue(), ...)})

This will prevent changes from input$value to propagate through debouncedValue until input$value has stopped changing for approximately 500 milliseconds.
